title: Elementary facts on the dual skeleton La: closedness, face centres, cone property (printed (1), (2))
statement: Notation: m, ℓ ∈ ℕ, d := m + 1 + ℓ, indices i range over Fin d, ℝ^d = Eucl d with the Euclidean norm |·|, C := [0,1]^d (y ∈ C iff 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i), a ∈ ℝ^d with 1/4 < a_i < 3/4 for all i, and La := {y ∈ ℝ^d : there is a set J of indices with |J| = m + 2 and integers k_i with y_i − a_i = k_i for all i ∈ J}. Then: (1) La is closed; (2) for every set J of indices with |J| ≥ m + 2 and every c ∈ ℝ^d with c_i = a_i for all i ∈ J, c ∈ La; (3) for every set J of indices, c, x, y ∈ ℝ^d and s ∈ ℝ such that c_i = a_i for i ∈ J, c_i ∈ {0,1} for i ∉ J, x_i = c_i for i ∉ J, y ∈ C, s > 0 and y_i − c_i = s·(x_i − c_i) for all i: if y ∈ La then x ∈ La. (Informal remark, not part of the statement: in (3), (J, c) describes a face of C with free coordinates J and centre c; (3) says that moving from x along the ray from the face centre to a point y of C does not create membership in La.)
